To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the throughput performance of adaptive modulation systems can be improved using ARQ schemes.
the throughput performance of the system degrades when outdated channel information is used.
the throughput of the system is maximized when the ARQ scheme is based on the channel quality of the strongest link.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of a selective-repeat AR-Q scheme based on adaptive M-QAM combined with selection transmit-diversity over Markovian-Nagakami channels.
the following issues: 1) The performance of the adaptive ARQ scheme is analyzed for both perfect and outdated channel state information.

the following: (a) the analysis of the throughput of an adaptive M-QAM ARQ system combined with selection diversity, (b) the analysis of packet error rate of an adaptive M- QAM ARQ system, and (c) the analysis of throughput and packet error rates of an adaptive MQAM ARQ system with outdated and imperfect channel state information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the adaptive ARQ system is not significantly degraded by using outdated and/or channel estimation errors, and that the system is quite robust against channel estimation errors.
, in the presence of outdated or imperfect CSI, adaptive ARQ schemes are not effective for throughput enhancement.

, the use of outdated and/or imperfect CSI in the adaptive M-QAM/selection transmit diversity ARQ system results in a significant performance degradation in terms of the throughput and packet error rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the throughput performance of ARQ scheme combined with adaptive modulation and selection transmit diversity is improved by the use of outdated channel information, but it is degraded by the use of imperfect channel information.
, in a fading environment, the throughput of the system is improved by increasing the number of transmit antennas and/or increasing the maximum number of retransmission attempts.
the proposed ARQ scheme is able to achieve a significant throughput enhancement over a wide range of channel conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a given packet error rate, the throughput of the adaptive ARQ system combined with transmit diversity is significantly higher compared to a nonadaptive ARQ system combined transmit diversity, especially when there is a high degree of channel variation.
, for a given packet size, the throughput of the ARQ system is maximized by using an M-QAM system with an optimal power allocation scheme and a selection transmit diversity scheme.
the performance degradation due to the outdated and/or imperfect CSI can be mitigated by using a proper ARQ scheme.
